children: iBio reported financial results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, posting revenue of $0.1 million and a net loss of $33.0 million. The company held approximately $88.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments as of June 30, 2026. iBio advanced multiple long-acting antibody programs into clinical or IND-enabling development during the year.
Revenue: $0.1 million for the year ended June 30, 2026 (versus $0.4 million in FY2025).
Operating loss: $(35.1) million for the year ended June 30, 2026.
Net loss: $(33.044) million for the year ended June 30, 2026 (comprehensive loss $33.089 million including unrealized loss on debt securities of $0.045 million).
R&D expense: $19.6 million for FY2026 (up from $8.3 million in FY2025); G&A expense: $10.6 million for FY2026.
Cash, cash equivalents and investments in debt securities: approximately $88.0 million as of June 30, 2026.

Initiated first-in-human Phase 1 trial for IBIO-600 (long-acting anti-myostatin antibody), completing single ascending dose dosing of 31 of 32 planned participants across four cohorts with no safety findings that precluded escalation; preparing to advance to multiple ascending dose portion.

Advanced IBIO-610 (long-acting Activin E antibody) into IND-enabling studies after preclinical results showing near-complete suppression of active Activin E for up to eight weeks in obese non-human primates and fat-selective weight loss in rodents; demonstrated additive effects with semaglutide and prevention of weight regain after GLP-1 discontinuation in preclinical models.

Selected a development candidate for IBIO-800 (myostatin × Activin A bispecific antibody) and initiated CMC and IND-enabling nonclinical development with an initial focus on pulmonary hypertension associated with HFpEF.

In-licensed AstralBio’s amylin receptor antibody program, adding a portfolio of selective AMY1/AMY3 receptor agonists and dual amylin/calcitonin receptor agonists now progressing through preclinical characterization.
Strengthened organizational capacity: appointed Molly Carr, M.D. as Chief Medical Officer and added Elizabeth Stoner, M.D. to the Board to support clinical development and capital markets expertise.
